newsitem.title: FRANCE: France keeps option for third Paris airport.
newsitem.headline: France keeps option for third Paris airport.

text.p: France's left-wing government on Thursday left open the possibility of building a third airport for Paris southwest of the capital despite opposition from the Greens members of the ruling coalition.
Communist Transport Minister Jean-Louis Gayssot told the Senate (upper house) that Orly airport to the south of Paris and Roissy-Charles de Gaulle to the north had reached saturation.
He said the government must be vigilant about safety standards and avoid traffic being diverted to rival airports in Amsterdam and Francfort.
"This is why, in the long-term, I will not shelve plans for the third airport," he said.
He said dialogue would continue over the proposed location at Beauvilliers, near Chartres, 80 km (50 miles) southwest of Paris, the site chosen by the previous conservative government.
The Greens, who hold the environment portfolio in the Socialist-led coalition, have opposed both building a third airport at Beauvilliers or expanding Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport.
A third airport would cost 50 billion to 100 billion francs ($10-$20 billion). The previous government had said work would not start before 2015.
